sections.h2: Where is Morgan County, Alabama, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Morgan County is in north-central Alabama along the Tennessee River, with Decatur as the county seat and largest city. It covers 599 square miles, of which 579 are land and 20 are water, according to the Census Bureau figures repeated on Wikipedia.

The neighbors are Madison County to the northeast, Marshall to the east, Cullman to the south, Lawrence to the west and Limestone to the northwest. Part of the Wheeler National Wildlife Refuge lies inside the county.

ItemMorgan County
CreatedFebruary 6, 1818 (as Cotaco County)
Renamed for Daniel MorganJune 14, 1821
County seatDecatur
2020 census population123,421
2025 estimate126,483
Housing units, 202053,265, with 7.6% vacant
Owner-occupied share, 202070.1% of occupied homes

Morgan County belongs to the Decatur metropolitan area and to the larger Huntsville, Decatur and Albertville combined statistical area.

The territorial legislature created the county in 1818 from land the Cherokee ceded in the Treaty of Turkeytown, and first called it Cotaco County. In 1821 lawmakers changed the name to honor Revolutionary War General Daniel Morgan of Virginia.

The population has risen every decade on record. The census counted 5,263 residents in 1820, 100,043 in 1990 and 123,421 in 2020, a gain of 3.3% from 2010. For a seller, steady growth of that kind usually means a continuing pool of buyers, though it says nothing about any single house.

sections.h2: Which cities and towns make up Morgan County?
sections.html:
The county has three cities and five towns, and a long list of smaller communities that sit outside any municipality.

  • Cities: Decatur, Hartselle, and Huntsville, which has some land in the county. Part of Decatur reaches into Limestone County.
  • Towns: Eva, Falkville, Priceville, Somerville and Trinity.
  • Unincorporated: Lacey's Spring, Valhermoso Springs, Union Hill, Danville, Neel, Ryan Crossroads and others.

Morgan County is a dry county, but alcohol sales are allowed inside Decatur, Hartselle and Priceville. That quirk has no bearing on a house sale. The location of a property relative to city limits does, since it decides which police, fire, utility and school services a buyer gets.

sections.h2: What does the 2020 census say about Morgan County households and housing?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 49,241 households in Morgan County, in 53,265 housing units. About 7.6% of those units were vacant, and of the occupied ones 70.1% were owner-occupied and 29.9% were rented.

More than a third of residents (38.4%) live in rural areas, so many Morgan County sellers own houses on larger lots or along county roads. About 18% of residents are 65 or older. A house passed to heirs who live in another town is a common reason an owner decides to sell.

sections.h2: What schools serve Morgan County homes?
sections.html:
Three public districts operate in the county: Decatur City Schools, Hartselle City Schools and Morgan County Schools. Which one a house falls under depends on the address, not on the mailing city, so check the district map before you tell a buyer anything.

Buyers with children often start their search by school district. If a house you own sits near a boundary line, put the district name in your listing or tell your cash buyer so there is no surprise later.

sections.h2: What roads, rail and river access does Morgan County have?
sections.html:
Interstate 65 runs through Morgan County, and U.S. 31, U.S. 72 Alternate and U.S. 231 provide the main surface routes. State Routes 24, 36, 67 and 157 carry local traffic.

  • Rail: CSX Transportation and Norfolk Southern both operate in the county.
  • River: the Tennessee River is the county's main waterway.
  • Neighbor: Madison County, with Huntsville, borders Morgan to the northeast.

Drive times to I-65 and to Huntsville differ a lot between Decatur and a rural address near the Cullman or Lawrence county lines, and a buyer will weigh that.

sections.h2: When are Morgan County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31. The Alabama Department of Revenue publishes the same calendar for every county, including Morgan.

WhenWhat happens
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes become delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilProperty advertised for sale
MayTax sale

The Morgan County courthouse stands in Decatur, and Wikipedia confirms Decatur as the county seat. Local offices handle assessment, collection and probate records, so a seller who needs a payoff number should contact the county office directly before listing or accepting an offer.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions apply in Morgan County?
sections.html:
The state homestead exemption covers a single-family owner-occupied home on up to 160 acres, if it was your main residence on the first day of the tax year. The state department says to apply at your county office.

  • Under 65 and not disabled: up to $4,000 of assessed value on the state portion.
  • Age 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or blind: no maximum on the state portion.
  • County exemptions: $2,000 of assessed value for most owners, with higher limits and income tests for seniors and for disabled owners.

The exemption belongs to the owner, not the house. A buyer starts without it until they apply, so a purchaser's first bill may be higher than the seller's was.

sections.h2: What deed tax applies when a Morgan County house sells?
sections.html:
Alabama charges a recordation tax of 50 cents for every $500 of value conveyed by a deed. The deed is recorded with the judge of probate, and the recording office asks for proof of the real price paid.

On a $190,000 sale, the arithmetic is 380 units of $500 at 50 cents each, or $190 in tax. State law gives two thirds of that tax to the state treasury and one third to the county. A mortgage on which the mortgage tax was already paid can reduce the taxable value.

Anyone who intentionally withholds proof of value after a request faces a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax due, whichever is greater.

sections.h2: What do Morgan County sellers run into, and where does a cash sale help?
sections.html:
Sellers in Morgan County often hold an older house, an inherited property or a rental that no longer pays its way. A cash sale that closes as-is helps when the work needed to list a house would cost more than the owner can spend.

  • Houses in Decatur and Hartselle with deferred repairs.
  • Inherited property in Falkville, Somerville or Priceville.
  • Rural parcels with a house on them, outside city services.
  • Owners behind on taxes who want to avoid the spring tax sale.

Cash Home Buyers looks at Morgan County houses in their current condition and responds with a written offer. If the number does not fit, you walk away with no obligation.

faqs.q: When are Morgan County, AL property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, with delinquency after December 31. The Alabama Department of Revenue says unpaid accounts go to probate court in February and are advertised in April before a May tax sale.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax in Morgan County, Alabama?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents for each $500 of value on the deed, set by Alabama Code 40-22-1. The probate judge's office collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Is Morgan County a dry county?
faqs.a: Yes, though alcohol sales are allowed in Decatur, Hartselle and Priceville. This has no effect on property tax or on selling a house.

faqs.q: Can I get a homestead exemption in Morgan County?
faqs.a: Yes, if the house is your primary residence on the first day of the tax year. Apply at the county office; the state exemption is up to $4,000 of assessed value for owners under 65.
